question: How do you write custom middleware in Django and what are the common use cases?
title: Django Custom Middleware
direct_answer: Django middleware is a class with __init__(get_response) called once at startup and __call__(request) called per request. Call self.get_response(request) to pass to the next middleware or view. Common use cases: request logging, adding response headers (CORS, request IDs), authentication token extraction, rate limiting, per-request database tenant selection, exception transformation.
interviewer_intent: Tests practical Django knowledge. Writing middleware shows understanding of the request lifecycle beyond just views.

sections.title: Middleware patterns
sections.content:
Middleware is a component that wraps the entire view pipeline. The new-style middleware (Django 1.10+) is a simple callable:

__init__(get_response): receives the next middleware or view callable. Called once when Django initializes. Use for one-time setup.
__call__(request): called for every request. Call get_response(request) to pass control to the rest of the chain. Code before: runs before the view. Code after: runs after the view.

Alternatively, override process_view(request, view_func, view_args, view_kwargs) to intercept after URL dispatch but before the view runs. process_exception(request, exception) handles view exceptions.

Common real-world middleware: request ID injection (generate UUID, attach to request, add to response header, put in logging context), multi-tenant routing (read tenant slug from domain, set on request), API key authentication (check header before view, attach user to request), response compression (gzip based on Accept-Encoding).

sections.title: Production middleware examples
Middleware rules
items: Call self.get_response(request) to continue — short-circuit by returning a response
process_exception: only called for view exceptions, not middleware exceptions
Order in MIDDLEWARE matters: earlier runs first on request, last on response
Middleware should be stateless — don't store per-request state on self

seo.metaTitle: Django Custom Middleware — Request ID, Rate Limiting, Exception Handling
seo.metaDescription: Write Django custom middleware: __init__ and __call__ pattern, before/after view code, process_exception, and production examples for request IDs and rate limiting.

speakable_v2.hook: Custom middleware is how you add cross-cutting concerns to every request without touching every view.

beats.content: The pattern: __init__ gets the next callable once at startup. __call__ runs per request — your before-view code, call get_response(), your after-view code. Short-circuit by returning a response without calling get_response.

items: Request ID injection for distributed tracing
API key extraction and user attachment before the view
Rate limiting with a cache backend
Exception transformation from Python errors to JSON responses

beats.content: Keep middleware stateless. Don't store request data on self — middleware is a singleton. Store per-request state on the request object instead.

speakable_v2.cap: Middleware vs signals: middleware is for request-level cross-cutting. Signals are for model events (post_save, pre_delete). Don't confuse them.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Django signals for model events, or how to scope middleware to specific URL patterns.
